Procedural boundary: the strongest pacemaker-implantation literature around bundle branch block arises after transcatheter aortic valve implantation, where the procedure itself causes the block; that evidence class is excluded from this edge's scope, which covers the spontaneous natural-history association in subjects without overt heart disease.
governanceNotes: Authored as ASSOCIATION_ONLY with NOT_ESTABLISHED consensus: a large matched-cohort study of atomic-bomb survivors (520 newly acquired right bundle branch block subjects without organic heart disease, 1,038 matched comparators) reports pacemaker implantation for high-degree atrioventricular block or sick sinus syndrome at roughly 4.8-fold higher hazard (6.3-fold when implanted for sick sinus syndrome), with axis deviation raising risk further; the progression literature for left bundle branch block is dominated by procedure-associated cohorts (post-TAVI), which are a different evidence class and were deliberately excluded.

Conservatism boundaries: the cohort association cannot identify which individual blocks progress, progression latency spans years to decades, and shared age-related degenerative substrate means the block may be a marker of conduction-system disease rather than its driver; implantation indicates advanced conduction disease, so the edge documents the documented progression association and requires electrophysiologic confirmation in every individual case.

Duplicate-scope check: no edges exist from this primary or into implantable-cardiac-pacemaker in the registry; the existing implantable-cardiac-pacemaker -> heart-valve-disorders edge is an outgoing edge from the device identity and is not duplicate scope for an incoming edge.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: A long-follow-up matched-cohort study within the Adult Health Study of atomic-bomb survivors detected 520 subjects with newly acquired complete right bundle branch block and no organic heart disease and matched them 1:2 to comparators without block; over follow-up extending to 2010, right bundle branch block carried a hazard ratio of 4.79 (95 percent CI 1.89-12.58) for pacemaker implantation for any cause, 3.77 (95 percent CI 1.09-13.07) when implanted for high-degree atrioventricular block, and 6.28 (95 percent CI 1.24-31.73) when implanted for sick sinus syndrome, with coexisting axis deviation roughly tripling the all-cause hazard; procedure-associated conduction injury cohorts (new left bundle branch block after transcatheter aortic valve implantation, with about 24 percent progressing to implantation) document the same progression phenomenon under iatrogenic conditions.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the cohort cannot distinguish the block as driver from the block as early marker of a shared degenerative conduction-system process, progression latency and individual trajectory are highly variable, implantation decisions are guideline- and clinician-dependent outcomes rather than pure disease endpoints, and competing drivers (ischemic disease, infiltrative disease, drug effects, hyperkalemia, thyroid dysfunction) require individual exclusion, so no directional claim is made here.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized progressive-degenerative-conduction pathway has been described: bundle branch block reflects slowed or failed conduction in the His-Purkinje system, commonly from age-related fibrotic change of the conduction tissue (Lenegre or Levasseur patterns) or from the same disease processes affecting the atrioventricular node and sinus node; under this pathway the visible block is the first electrocardiographic surface of a progressive process that later compromises remaining conduction pathways or sinus node function, culminating in high-degree atrioventricular block or sick sinus syndrome that meets pacing criteria; the matched-cohort progression association would fit this shared-substrate progression, but fibrosis burden is not directly measured in the cohort data, the block may equally be a marker rather than the anatomic predecessor of the later block site, and diffuse disease, ischemia, infiltrative disease, and drug effects remain active competing explanations, so no directional claim is made here.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Bundle branch block co-occurs with substantially elevated future pacemaker implantation rates in cohort data, but individual determination requires serial electrocardiographic documentation establishing the block with chronology, electrophysiologic or rhythm documentation of the advanced conduction disease that prompted implantation, device records identifying the implantation indication, and exclusion of ischemic, infiltrative, drug-induced, metabolic, and thyroid contributors, all reviewed case by case by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Serial electrocardiograms or Holter documentation establishing bundle branch block with acquisition chronology; electrophysiologic study or telemetry documentation of high-degree atrioventricular block or sinus-node dysfunction with the implanation indication recorded; pacemaker interrogation reports; transthoracic imaging and laboratory workup excluding structural, ischemic, infiltrative, metabolic, and drug causes; a medical professional's opinion connecting the documented findings in this individual case
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Ischemic heart disease causing both the block and subsequent advanced conduction disease
Infiltrative disease (cardiac sarcoidosis, amyloidosis) as the shared substrate
Drug effects (atrioventricular nodal blockers, digoxin) and hyperkalemia provoking advanced block
Hypothyroidism or hypothermia-related conduction slowing unrelated to the block

suggestions.rationale: Authored conservatively at association-only strength: the pacemaker-implantation association is cohort-documented with tightly bounded confidence intervals, but the block-as-driver versus block-as-marker question is unresolved, the strongest procedural literature is iatrogenic and out of scope, and individual progression is unpredictable, so this edge flags the documented progression association for evidence-gap review only and must never be presented as established causation or aggravation.

sourceReferences.citation: Kusumoto S, Kawano H, Makita N, et al. Right bundle branch block without overt heart disease predicts higher risk of pacemaker implantation: the study of atomic-bomb survivors. Int J Cardiol. 2014;174(1):77-82. PMID 24745858. doi:10.1016/j.ijcard.2014.03.152.
sourceReferences.note: Matched cohort (520 newly acquired right bundle branch block subjects without organic heart disease versus 1,038 matched comparators) reporting pacemaker implantation hazards of 4.79 all-cause, 3.77 for atrioventricular block, and 6.28 for sick sinus syndrome, with axis deviation tripling risk; the abstract frames the finding as progression association and explicitly notes that progression mechanisms differ with and without axis deviation, supporting the association-strength framing.
